content:
The compass_log table with the user_override column is T2Helix's most load-bearing design choice — observed by Anthony 2026-05-10 during v0.0.1 review. The methodology IS the product.

Every PreToolUse classification (WITNESS / PAUSE / OPEN) creates a compass_log row. When a user disagrees with a classification ("you should not have stopped me there" or "you should have stopped me there"), the override gets logged in the user_override column. After meaningful dogfood time, this produces empirical, longitudinal, first-person data on which rules fire correctly and which need refinement.

This is the same methodology that drove the relational coupling experiment (3,830 inference runs across 5 architectures): orthogonalize the variables, log everything, let the data speak. Applied to product use, it becomes: orthogonalize the rules (each rule a separate match), log every fire, let user behavior reveal which rules are calibrated to user reality vs which are author-projection.

The widen-don't-flip pattern is the discipline that uses this data correctly: when a rule misfires, the response is to refine the rule (narrow its match, soften its classification, or add a context exception) — never to flip the rule's polarity. Calibration compounds; whipsaws don't.

Why this is load-bearing for the product story: T2Helix is presentable to outside readers (Fellows program, METR audience) not just as "a useful Claude Code plugin" but as "a product that embeds longitudinal first-person methodology in its operation." Every install becomes a measurement instrument, with consent, locally, on the user's machine. The chronicle is not a feature; it is the substrate. The compass_log is not a logging table; it is the calibration mechanism.

This entry is hypothesis-layer because the methodology has not yet been validated under real dogfood conditions — only in scaffolded smoke tests. Convert to ground_truth after first week of real usage shows compass_log + user_override producing the predicted refinement signal.
